– the failing test (signature + snippet),

– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: 
The current bug report indicates an "endless loop" when calling the asPath() method on a node with a reset default namespace (empty namespace) within an XML structure where the default namespace is overridden to empty in a child element.

Analyzing the asPath() method of NodePointer:
- The method first checks if the parent is a container (parent.isContainer()) and, if so, returns parent.asPath().
- Otherwise, it recursively builds the path by prepending the parent's asPath() to the current node name.
- The parent pointer is obtained with getParent(), which skips container parents to find the actual parent pointer by looping through container parents via getImmediateParentPointer().
- The isContainer() method in NodePointer always returns false, meaning no node is recognized as a container by default.

The bug refers to an endless loop during asPath(), which in the method occurs only if the parent is a container and keeps calling parent.asPath() infinitely.

Because isContainer() returns false, the logic in getParent() skips container parents, potentially resulting in the parent pointer being set to the same node repeatedly or in a cycle in case of improper namespace reset nodes.

The XML snippet example shows:
- A b:foo element with xmlns:b="bla" and xmlns="test111"
- A child <test> element with xmlns="" (empty namespace)

It is likely that when namespaces are reset, the NodePointer's parent chain or container status is misrepresented, causing getParent() to loop incorrectly or return a node whose asPath() again calls parent.asPath() endlessly.

This is consistent with the bug report description of an endless loop when requesting .asPath() on nodes with reset default namespaces.

Hence, the root cause likely lies in the interplay of parent navigation (getParent()), handling of container nodes (isContainer()), and namespace reset nodes, which leads to cyclic or infinite parent linking or mistaken container detection triggering the endless loop in asPath().

The failing test tries to reproduce this by calling doTest("b:foo/test", DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM, "/b:foo[1]/test[1]") which involves the XPath "b:foo/test" that corresponds to a child node "test" under "b:foo", with likely the "test" element in empty default namespace scenario. This triggers the .asPath() call on that node, causing the infinite loop due to the parent container logic.

In conclusion, the asPath() method's reliance on parent.isContainer() and the getParent() skipping container parents is not robust when default namespaces are reset on child nodes, leads to an endless loop.

This diagnosis aligns fully with the current bug report's symptom of endless loop in asPath() due to default namespace reset and node parent navigation.

No recent bug reports provide additional evidence or fixes relevant here.

# Summary:
- asPath() uses parent.isContainer() to decide how to assemble the path.
- isContainer() always false in NodePointer by default.
- getParent() skips container parents via a loop.
- Reset default namespace causes incorrect parent or container handling on nodes.
- This causes a cyclic or endless call chain in asPath(), leading to infinite loop.

This is the root cause of the failure seen in the test testInnerEmptyNamespaceDOM().

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
